method: Verification of the round-2 fix commit against the working tree, by command. Round-2 findings preserved verbatim at reviews/review-findings-plan-r2.json. reviews/consensus-plan.json was not consulted.

findings.title: The blocking pull_request sweep reds every PR whose branch is not openspec/<change-id>
findings.description:
Critical: the C3 fix made an active change id mandatory for the blocking run but never said what that run does on a PR that has no change id, so as planned it fails every unrelated PR. spec.md:509-511 states 'The blocking run SHALL resolve requirement identifiers exactly as change scope does ... and SHALL therefore require an active change id, failing rather than inferring one.' tasks.md:582-584 states 'the pull_request job MUST pass --change <id> derived from the branch (openspec/<change-id>).' Nothing in spec.md, design.md, tasks.md or work-packages.yaml states the behavior when the branch is not of that form.

Demonstrated: `sed -n 1,12p .github/workflows/ci.yml` shows the workflow triggers on `pull_request:` and `merge_group:` with no branch filter. `git branch -r` returns, among 40+ refs, origin/dependabot/pip/agent-coordinator/jsonschema-gte-4.26.0, origin/dependabot/github_actions/actions/upload-artifact-7, origin/claude/tech-debt-analysis-skill-IdbCE, origin/chore/subagent-dispatch-authorization and origin/codex/explore-interactive-code-visualization-options. Each of those raises a PR. Under the plan the blocking sweep job runs on each, cannot derive a change id, and per the spec's own fail-closed rule must fail rather than infer one. That reds every dependabot, claude/*, chore/* and codex/* PR the day task 5.7 lands — the same 'reds the tree the day it is installed' failure that finding C2 was raised and fixed to avoid, reintroduced on a different axis.

Two further instances of the same unstated case: (a) agent branches are `openspec/<change-id>--<agent-id>` (docs/guides/worktree-management.md:11 — 'Agent branches use `--` separator ... git cannot have both refs/heads/a/b and refs/heads/a/b/c'), so a naive parse yields `<change-id>--<agent-id>`, which names no directory under openspec/changes/ and also fails to resolve; (b) the `merge_group` trigger runs on a synthetic queue ref that is neither form.
findings.resolution: State the branch-to-change-id resolution rule and the non-resolving case normatively. Suggested: strip any trailing `--<agent-id>` before resolving; when the branch does not name an existing `openspec/changes/<id>` directory, print an explicit SKIP naming the branch and exit zero — the same detection-plus-printed-SKIP shape the skill-workflow delta just adopted (specs/skill-workflow/spec.md:36-39) — or run that PR in the non-blocking union mode. Carry the rule into task 5.7's notes together with the job-level `if:` condition, and into the requirement in specs/gen-eval-framework/spec.md so it survives archive.

findings.title: The two capability-scope resolution modes have no implementing or testing task, and their scenario is owned by a package that cannot write the gate
findings.description:
Critical: the C3 fix added normative behavior to the spec but did not carry it into the task or package decomposition, so no package both owns the behavior and can write the code. spec.md:509-517 now requires two distinct capability-scope resolution modes (blocking run = archive shadowed by the active change's delta, requires a change id; post-merge run = archive shadowed by every delta under openspec/changes/).

Demonstrated: `grep -n -- '--scope|--change' tasks.md` returns hits only at 435-436, 561-562, 583, 630 and 636. Within wp-gate's task range (3.1-3.16) the only statement is task 3.16's note at tasks.md:435-439: 'one gate, a --scope change|capability argument. Change scope requires --change <id> (no inference across the ~34 live change dirs) ... capability scope reads everything.' An implementer building from that writes --change as change-scope-only. Nothing there mentions two capability resolution modes.

`grep -n "blocking-sweep-requires-a-change-id|candidate's own delta" tasks.md work-packages.yaml` returns exactly one hit: tasks.md:578, the Spec scenarios line of task 5.7. Task 5.7 belongs to wp-wiring (work-packages.yaml:392, 'Tasks 5.6-5.9'), whose scope.write_allow (work-packages.yaml:453-461) is skills/validate-feature/SKILL.md, skills/tests/validate-feature/**, skills/pyproject.toml, .github/workflows/ci.yml, packages/gen-eval/README.md and packages/gen-eval/DOWNSTREAM.md. The gate itself, packages/gen-eval/scripts/check_traceability.py, is wp-gate's (work-packages.yaml:241) and is not writable by wp-wiring. The package claiming the scenario cannot implement it.

No test task covers it either: wp-gate's test-file mapping is explicit and closed at work-packages.yaml:260-262 — 'test_traceability_gate.py <- 3.1-3.6; test_traceability_wording.py <- 3.8; test_capability_scope.py <- 3.9, 3.11, 3.13; test_change_scope.py <- 3.15. No fifth file.' Task 3.15 is change-scoped evaluation. Capability-scope resolution has no test home.

Concrete downstream break: wp-gate depends only on wp-model and is dispatched before wp-wiring, so it ships argparse first. If it implements --change as change-scope-only, task 5.7c's acceptance command at tasks.md:630 — `check_traceability.py --scope capability --change trace-requirements-to-contracts` — is rejected outright, and 5.7c is the change's only stated acceptance criterion.
findings.resolution: Write both resolution modes into task 3.16's note (capability scope accepts an optional --change; with it, shadow the archive with that delta and resolve identically to change scope; without it, shadow with every delta present under openspec/changes/). Add a test task under wp-gate covering both modes, and amend the 'No fifth file' mapping accordingly or fold the coverage into test_capability_scope.py. Move the `blocking-sweep-requires-a-change-id` scenario claim from task 5.7 to that gate task, leaving 5.7 to claim only the CI-wiring scenarios it can actually implement.

findings.title: New scenario asserts a gate behavior no implementation can satisfy and that contradicts the post-merge run
findings.description:
Critical: the scenario added by the C3 fix ends with '- **AND** the sweep SHALL fail rather than run when no active change id is supplied' (spec.md:548-551). At capability scope the absence of --change is precisely the post-merge run's signature — eleven lines earlier the same requirement says 'The post-merge run has no active change; it SHALL resolve against the archived specs shadowed by every spec delta present under openspec/changes/ on the integration branch' (spec.md:512-514). Both cannot hold: a gate that fails whenever no change id is supplied can never execute the post-merge run at all.

The gate has no other input by which to distinguish the two contexts. `grep -n -- '--scope|--change' spec.md design.md tasks.md` finds no third discriminator anywhere — no --blocking, no --mode, no run-context argument. Task 5.7's own note pushes the other way (tasks.md:601-604): 'even for capability scope, keep the invocation bare ... A gate whose two call sites disagree on argv reports failure on a correct tree.'

This is not only awkward phrasing. This change maps every scenario to a task and a test (see every '**Spec scenarios**:' line in tasks.md), and no test can be written for a clause that must never fire on a correct implementation. It also lands in specs/gen-eval-framework/spec.md, the one artifact that survives archive — the exact failure class round 2 was raised about. The neighbouring `unresolvable-scope-errors` scenario (spec.md:483-489) shows the correct construction: it explicitly scopes itself to 'a change-scoped run'.
findings.resolution: Rewrite the clause so its subject is the caller rather than the gate — e.g. '**AND** the CI job running the blocking sweep SHALL supply the active change id, so citations to the candidate's own new requirements are not reported as unresolved' — and leave the fail-closed assertion with `unresolvable-scope-errors`, where it is scoped to change-scoped runs and is implementable. If the intent really is a gate-level assertion, then a second discriminator (an explicit run-context flag) has to be introduced in spec.md, task 3.16 and task 5.7 together, and the 'keep the invocation bare' note reconciled with it.

findings.title: Task 5.7's 'keep the invocation bare' note contradicts the mandatory --change <id> in the same task
findings.description: Task 5.7's first note now requires the pull_request job to pass --change <id> derived from the branch (tasks.md:582-584); its fifth note still says 'even for capability scope, keep the invocation bare, as with generate_tool_descriptor.py --check' (tasks.md:601-604). The two CI jobs also necessarily differ in argv — the blocking one carries --change, the post-merge one by definition cannot — so the note's stated rationale ('a gate whose two call sites disagree on argv reports failure on a correct tree') no longer describes this gate. Residue of the C3 fix not sweeping the older notes in the same task.
findings.resolution: Reword to the point the note is actually protecting, which task 5.6 states correctly at tasks.md:567-568: 'run it BARE, never piped. A pipeline's $? is the last stage's status.' Drop or qualify the 'bare argv' framing.

findings.title: wp-wiring's PREFLIGHT is not the agent's first instruction, and in the local-parallel tier it never reaches the agent
findings.description:
C5's substantive defect is genuinely fixed: the 'ENFORCED by a verification step' claim is gone, work-packages.yaml:405-423 now says plainly that the DAG cannot express the precondition, and the ordering claim it rests on checks out — skills/implement-feature/SKILL.md:395 describes Phase B as 'code generation within scope, deterministic scope check via git diff, verification steps', so verification does run last. What remains is a smaller overstatement of the same kind.

The text claims 'the FIRST instruction to the agent implementing this package is to run the preflight command below and stop ... before reading anything else or editing any file.' Two checkable problems: (a) the PREFLIGHT block is the LAST paragraph of the description (work-packages.yaml:434-437), after roughly thirty lines of rationale, so it is not first even for a reader given the whole description; (b) in the local-parallel tier the worker never receives the description at all — the dispatch prompt template at skills/implement-feature/SKILL.md:325-347 has exactly four slots (File Scope, Context, Verification, Scope Discipline) and no package-description slot, and the Context Slicing table at SKILL.md:641-646 lists proposal/design/contracts/package scope, not the description. `grep -rn description skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/package_executor.py` returns nothing; that module builds results, not prompts. The description does reach a coordinated-tier worker, via dag_scheduler.py:139 (input_data.package.description) and dag_scheduler.py:175 (the work-queue task description), so the claim is tier-conditional rather than false everywhere.
findings.resolution: Address the precondition to the orchestrator, which demonstrably does read work-packages.yaml, and move the PREFLIGHT block to the top of the description. One sentence suffices: 'The orchestrator MUST run the preflight below before dispatching this package — the local-parallel worker prompt template carries no package description, so this cannot be delegated to the worker.' Keep the post-hoc verification step as detection, as the current text correctly distinguishes.

findings.title: The ratchet's 'cannot grow' claim is not enforced by any CI check
findings.description: spec.md:591-593 says 'Reporting the existing one while failing any newly added one is the ratchet: the debt is visible and cannot grow.' But the failing half exists only in change scope (spec.md:576-578, 'change scope SHALL fail on it only when the diff adds or modifies it'), and change scope is wired into /validate-feature, whose trigger D12's table records as 'local / pre-PR' (design.md:411). CI's blocking job runs at capability scope, which reports and does not fail on misplaced instances. So nothing in CI stops a PR that adds a root-misplaced instance. That is defensible — /validate-feature is a mandatory workflow phase in this repo — but 'cannot grow' overstates what is mechanically enforced.
findings.resolution: Qualify to 'cannot grow through the validated workflow', or state explicitly that the newly-added case is caught at validation time rather than in CI, so a reader does not infer a CI guarantee that is not there.

findings.title: D12's heading still states the position its own body refutes
findings.description: design.md:404 reads '### D12 — At validation the gate is diff-scoped; the full sweep runs on main'. The body ten lines below refutes exactly that (design.md:414-423): the blocking sweep runs on pull_request, and the push-on-main run is explicitly non-blocking. A reader skimming decision headings — which is how the decision index and the docs/decisions timeline present them — gets the pre-fix answer.
findings.resolution: Retitle to something like 'D12 — At validation the gate is diff-scoped; the blocking sweep runs on the merge candidate'.

findings.title: C1 verified closed — the spec delta states both run contexts and matches D12's table
findings.description: `grep -n 'on push|every push|merge candidate|post-merge|integration branch' spec.md` no longer returns either refuted sentence. The requirement now reads 'A full-capability evaluation SHALL run as a blocking check on the merge candidate, and SHALL run again, explicitly non-blocking, on the integration branch after merge' (spec.md:501-505), which matches D12's table rows at design.md:410-413 (pull_request = 'Opted-in surfaces block'; push on main = 'No — reports only'). The trailing rationale was replaced with D12's corrected reasoning (spec.md:523-525). `grep -i 'push|sweep runs|pull_request|schedule' proposal.md` returns one unrelated hit at line 168, so no stale claim survives there either.

findings.title: C4 verified closed — structural instance identification checks out against the real tree
findings.description: yaml.safe_load on openspec/contracts/gen-eval-framework/cli/gen-eval.yaml returns top-level keys ['contract_version', 'tool', 'commands', 'exit_codes'] — `tool` is genuinely a top-level key, as the rule requires and as tasks.md:321-323 records. yaml.safe_load on openspec/contracts/code-search/v2.yaml returns ['openapi', 'info', 'paths', 'components'] — top-level `openapi`, so the ratchet's motivating instance is correctly identified by the structural rule. `find openspec/contracts -maxdepth 2 -type f` returns exactly three files: code-search/README.md, code-search/v2.yaml, contracts/README.md — so README.md is the only other root-level file, and it is excluded twice over (not .yaml/.yml/.json, and named explicitly at spec.md:558-560). `find openspec -name traceability-exclusions.yaml` returns nothing: none exists yet, so the current tree cannot trip the D13 switch either.

findings.title: C6 verified closed — all three surfaces agree that 5.7c is [human] and owned by no package
findings.description: Surface 1, tasks.md:498-503: 'Tasks 5.1, 5.2, 5.3, and 5.7c are [human] ... Tasks 5.4-5.9 are engineering (wp-matrix and wp-wiring) with the single exception of 5.7c, which sits inside that numeric range but is owned by no package.' Surface 2, tasks.md:623: '- [ ] 5.7c [human] The unmutated tree passes at capability scope'. Surface 3, work-packages.yaml:392: 'Tasks 5.6-5.9, EXCEPT 5.7c which is [human] and owned by no package', reinforced by the carve-out comment block at work-packages.yaml:513-532 which names 4.1, 4.2, 4.2b, 5.1, 5.2, 5.3 and 5.7c and closes with 'wp-wiring's description states the range as 5.6-5.9 EXCEPT 5.7c'. No contradiction remains on any surface.

findings.title: C2 verified closed on the report-vs-fail ratchet; the newly-added case is stated where an implementer will find it
findings.description: The failing half is stated in the implementer-facing place. Task 3.6's note (tasks.md:307-323) gives three lettered assertions: '(a) the sweep REPORTS a pre-existing root instance naming the file and the expected location and exits zero on that account; (b) change scope FAILS when the diff adds or modifies a root instance; (c) README.md and traceability-exclusions.yaml at a capability root are not instances.' Task 3.6's Spec scenarios line (tasks.md:292) claims all three new scenarios, so they are owned by wp-gate, which can write both the gate and its tests. design.md:175-194 agrees, and `grep -i 'misplaced|capability root|v2.yaml' design.md proposal.md` surfaces no surviving 'fails the gate' statement. The residual overclaim in the spec's rationale is tracked separately as finding 6.

findings.title: Both non-blocking round-2 fixes check out
findings.description: Task 2.0 (tasks.md:142-146) now runs `python3 skills/project-context-refresh/scripts/cli.py refresh --producer api.contracts` rather than `make context-refresh`, which keeps the write inside wp-model's write_allow. The skill-workflow SKIP path is coherent end to end: the requirement carries the SKIP sentence (specs/skill-workflow/spec.md:36-39), a new scenario 'Gate absent in a consumer repository' was added, the wiring-tests scenario gained a matching AND clause, and task 5.6's Spec scenarios line was updated to 'all four scenarios' — so the new scenario is owned rather than orphaned. The claimed precedent is real: `grep -n -i skip skills/validate-feature/SKILL.md` shows the existing detect-then-print-SKIP shape at lines 180-182, 263-265 and 297-298.

findings.title: Deterministic gates pass
findings.description: `npx @fission-ai/openspec validate trace-requirements-to-contracts --strict` returns "Change 'trace-requirements-to-contracts' is valid". `agent-coordinator/.venv/bin/python skills/validate-packages/scripts/validate_work_packages.py openspec/changes/trace-requirements-to-contracts/work-packages.yaml` returns 'work-packages validation: VALID' with schema, depends_on_refs, dag_cycles and lock_keys all passing. Neither gate reaches findings 1-3, which is expected: all three are cross-artifact consistency and scenario-to-owner assignment, neither of which either gate models.

findings.title: consensus-plan.json remains unreliable and was not consulted
findings.description: Per the round-3 brief, the round-1 synthesizer reported blocking_count: 0 while ten blocking findings were live — a lexical-similarity artifact. It was ignored entirely for this round. Round 2's findings are preserved verbatim at openspec/changes/trace-requirements-to-contracts/reviews/review-findings-plan-r2.json.
